title: Publishers finally have AI buyers for their content yet zero say in the price
Why Layering a Specialist Bot & Agent Trust Solution With Your CDN Is Now Essential
summary:
When setting up a home theater, you start with a massive TV, right? 75-inch, minimum. 

But crank the TV volume as high as you like, and the sound is likely going to leave you underwhelmed, whether you’re watching a movie or a football game. You need at least a quality soundbar, or even better, a full surround sound system.

Built-in speakers are fine for basic viewing. But for sound that matches the picture, you need to layer dedicated, best-of-breed products.

The same principle applies to cybersecurity. For years, enterprises have relied on their CDNs, with integrated WAFs and basic bot management, as a primary defense against automated traffic. That made sense when many threats were relatively simple and manageable with rules-based or rate-limiting-dependent approaches. 

The reality today, however, is very different, and prominent analyst firms have explicitly recognized that in their latest research. In fact, Gartner recently wrote:

title: DataDome Recognized on Fast Company’s Next Big Things in Tech List
summary:
The annual list honors groundbreaking technologies with the potential to reshape industries and redefine the way we work and live

New York, NY, October 6, 2026 — DataDome, the leader in bot and agent trust management, today announced that Agent Trust has been named to Fast Company’s Next Big Things in Tech, an annual list recognizing breakthrough technologies with the potential to transform industries and shape the future.

Agent Trust was selected for giving businesses real-time visibility and control over AI agent behavior by assessing what agents intend to do, not just who they claim to be. A key component of DataDome’s platform, Agent Trust assigns every AI agent a dynamic, continuously updated 100-point score informed by 5 trillion signals analyzed daily.

“Identity tells you who is knocking at the door, but not what they’ll do once inside. With Agent Trust, we built the intent layer that gives businesses continuous control over AI agents, from the first request to the last,”  said Gilles Walbrou, CTO of DataDome. “Every agent gets a trust score that updates as its behavior changes, so businesses can welcome the agents that create value and stop the ones that don’t. Being recognized by Fast Company shows the market is ready for that shift.”

title: AI Traffic Is Up 82%. Can You Tell Which Agents to Trust?
summary:
AI agents are changing how people search, shop, and research online. They are also changing the security challenge for businesses.

Between July 2025 and June 2026, DataDome detected 52.7 billion AI agent and LLM crawler requests across our customer base. AI traffic grew 82.3% over the same time period, and its share of total web requests rose from 1.2% to 1.7%.

AI traffic isn’t one thing. Some agents fetch public information for users. Others collect content at scale or act inside authenticated journeys. A name alone doesn’t tell you which one you’re dealing with.

The State of Bot & Agent Security Report 2026 shows how AI traffic is growing more sophisticated and targeting deeper into the customer journey, making visibility essential.
